title_en: Pan Fengcai and Shi Xiwen — dereliction of duty case
keywords_en: criminal; dereliction of duty; first instance; grassroots people's court; Beijing; natural person; criminal law; determination of dereliction of duty; calculation of losses; supporting the plaintiff; rotting of garlic sprouts; freezing damage to cabbage; unauthorized modification of processing quota; concealment of losses
full_text_en:
People v. Pan Fengcai and Shi Xiwen — dereliction of duty

Defendant: Pan Fengcai, male, forty-five years old, formerly Party Branch Secretary and Director of the Nanyuan Vegetable Cold Storage of Beijing Vegetable Company. Arrested on April 9, 1986.

Defendant: Shi Xiwen, male, forty-six years old, formerly Deputy Director of the Nanyuan Vegetable Cold Storage of Beijing Vegetable Company. Arrested on April 9, 1986.

In March 1985, the defendants Pan Fengcai, Shi Xiwen, and Wang Louzeng (formerly Party Branch Secretary and Deputy Director of the Nanyuan Cold Storage, handled in a separate case) discussed and planned to purchase 3 million to 3.2 million jin (jin, 1 jin = 0.5 kg) of garlic sprouts. In early April, when the shift leaders and group leaders discussed the garlic sprout purchase plan, most disagreed, believing the plan exceeded the cold storage's processing and storage capacity, and reminded the leaders to heed the lesson of the major losses caused to the state in 1982 by over-purchasing. However, Pan, Shi, and Wang still insisted on purchasing garlic sprouts according to the original plan.

Before the garlic sprouts entered the storage, Pan Fengcai, Shi Xiwen, and Wang Louzeng, in violation of the operational rules for garlic sprout storage, unauthorizedly modified the processing methods and quotas for garlic sprouts, deciding to change from fine processing to coarse processing, and raised the daily processing quota per person from 300 to 350 jin to 700 jin. Each processing shift leader reported that the quota was too high and that coarse processing had no standard and was difficult to control. Pan, Shi, and Wang then proposed a decision that failure to meet the quota would result in deduction of bonuses and wages, and that for every 2 jin processed above the quota, an additional one cent would be paid. In May and June, large quantities of garlic sprouts were delivered to the storage. The workers, fearing bonus deductions, processed roughly, with an average daily processing of 2,000 jin, and some days processing reached as high as 3,970 jin. Due to the rough processing, good and bad garlic sprouts were stored together, creating a hidden risk of rot.

In July, when the Municipal Vegetable Company sent personnel to inspect the work of the Nanyuan Cold Storage, they discovered that wicker baskets were used for storing the garlic sprouts, and suggested reprocessing the garlic sprouts and replacing the wicker baskets with plastic baskets, storing them in the underground storage. Pan, Shi, and Wang took no measures in response to this. Subsequently, Zhang Xi'en and others from the refrigeration team and storage shifts submitted a written report, reflecting that in bays 202 and 305 the coils were not frosting, and the temperatures were above 1°C to 5°C, and recommended immediate measures. Pan and Shi ignored the report from Zhang Xi'en and others. At the end of August, white mold grew on the wicker baskets, and each storage shift leader reported this to Pan Fengcai and Shi Xiwen, urging prompt removal of the garlic sprouts. In September, some garlic sprouts in the underground storage showed signs of rot, and the storage shift leaders again reported to the leadership. At the same time, technical consultant Li Weijun repeatedly urged the removal of the garlic sprouts. Pan Fengcai said: "Our cold storage is a place to support people." To make Pan and Shi (Wang Louzeng had been transferred) change their stance, Li Weijun cut out a news item from the Economic Daily about the rot of 200,000 jin of vegetables in a Tianjin cold storage and gave it to Pan Fengcai. On September 17, when the "Five Stresses, Four Beauties, and Three Loves" Office of the Beijing Vegetable Company inspected the work, it discovered the rotten garlic sprouts and issued a briefing. Pan Fengcai and Shi Xiwen ignored all these opinions. When many units from Daxing, Petrochemical, and other places came to the storage to purchase garlic sprouts, Pan and Shi, disregarding market conditions, insisted on high prices, causing them to return empty trucks. In December, garlic sprouts in bay 305 began to rot, and an employee proactively contacted a buyer to sell 4,000 jin to reduce state losses. But Shi Xiwen still insisted on a high price, causing the deal to fall through.

On December 26, Pan Fengcai, despite the extensive rot of the garlic sprouts in the cold storage, took the finance section head, the large warehouse head, and three others on a pleasure trip to Guangzhou, Hangzhou, Shanghai, and other places on the pretext of contacting for equipment to make fried potato chips.

Due to the above reasons, over 334,900 jin of garlic sprouts rotted, and over 548,000 jin were sold at reduced prices, resulting in a total loss of over RMB 280,000 based on the purchase cost.

To cover up the fact of the garlic sprouts rotting, Pan Fengcai and Shi Xiwen did not report the truth to their superiors. Starting from January 22, 1986, they organized a so-called "dare-to-die squad," using trucks over three nights to transport over 90,000 jin of rotten garlic sprouts to a nearby large pit and buried them with a bulldozer.

Furthermore, in December 1985, due to the defendants Pan Fengcai and Shi Xiwen's irresponsibility in their work, over 530,000 jin of winter-stored Chinese cabbage in the cold storage were frozen to varying degrees. Of this, over 200,000 jin were given free to other units, and the rest was sold at reduced prices, causing a state loss of over RMB 22,900.

The above facts are confirmed by witness testimony, documentary evidence, and on-site investigation photos, and both defendants have confessed.

The Fengtai District People's Court of Beijing found during trial that the defendants Pan Fengcai and Shi Xiwen, serving as Director and Deputy Director of the Nanyuan Cold Storage of the Beijing Vegetable Company, caused major losses to the state and the people's interests due to their severe irresponsibility in their work, resulting in the rot of a large quantity of garlic sprouts and the freezing of Chinese cabbage. Their actions constituted the crime of dereliction of duty as provided for in Article 187 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China and should be punished. Pan Fengcai, as the cold storage director, and Shi Xiwen, as the deputy director in charge of business, bore primary and important responsibility respectively for the rot of the garlic sprouts. At the same time, in accordance with Article 57 of the Criminal Law, based on the facts of their crimes, the nature and circumstances of their crimes, and the harm caused to society, the court determined their sentences. Accordingly, on June 4, 1986, the court sentenced defendant Pan Fengcai to two years' imprisonment for the crime of dereliction of duty; and sentenced defendant Shi Xiwen to one year and six months' imprisonment for the crime of dereliction of duty.

After the judgment was pronounced, both defendants Pan Fengcai and Shi Xiwen stated that they accepted the judgment and would not appeal.
